Seismic ground motions will be affected by the geotechnical and dynamic characteristics of the different soil layers overlying the bedrock. The procedure by which the ground motions at the surface level are determined is known as the dynamic site response. The site response spectra must be obtained for the specific geotechnical conditions of the foundation soil of each project facility. The estimation of dynamic site response can be achieved by utilizing a multi-period amplification factor that is dependent on the average shear-wave velocity $\bar{v}_S$, as outlined in ASCE/SEI 7-22. The model proposed by @Stewart2017 is a three-component model dependent on shear-wave velocities $\bar v_S$ and can be used for both hard rock with $v_{ref}$ of 3000 m/s or soft rock with $v_{ref}$ of 760 m/s reference values.

$$\mathrm{ln}\ F(T_n,\bar v_S) \approx \beta_{BC} +\beta_{A} +\beta_{NL}+\varepsilon_F$${#eq-AF}

where $\beta_{BC}$ is a scaling term relative to $\bar v_S$ = 760 m/s, $\beta_{A}$ is amplification at $\bar v_S$ = 760 m/s relative to $v_{ref}$ = 3000 m/s and $\beta_{NL}$ is a factor that considers non-linear effects, which has strong influence in soft-soil conditions. The error term $\varepsilon_F$ from [@Stewart2017] is a log-normal random variable, with mean $E[\varepsilon]\approx 0$ and variance $\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon]\approx \sigma_F^2$. ^[Because the spectral ordinates in rock are actually random variables, with conditional expectation $s_a(T_n)$ and variance $\sigma_A^2$, the error term from this model has been adapted to incorporate the seismic hazard's uncertainty:
$$\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon_F]\approx \sigma_F^2+\sigma_{A}^2$$]


The site response spectra are obtained from the combination of the rock response spectra with the multiple period amplification factors, as established in ASCE/SEI 7-22.  For a target service level, defined by the Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP), and a given structural period $T_n$, the median spectral ordinates $S_a(T_n,\bar{v}_S)$ expected at sites characterized by an average shear-wave velocity $\bar{v}_S$, can be derived from the spectral ordinates on rock, denoted as $S_a(T_n)^o$. This approach facilitates a tailored response analysis based on arbitrary geotechnical site conditions.

$$S_a(T_n,\bar v_S) \approx F(T_n,\bar v_S) \ S_a(T_n,v_{ref})$${#eq-SAS}

where $F(T_n,\bar v_S)$ is the multi-period site factor and $S_a(T_n,v_{ref})$ is the spectral ordinate for the structural period $T_n$ for $\bar v_S=\bar v_{ref}$. Following the same approach, Peak-ground velocities $pgv^{sc}$ Arias intensities $a_i^{sc}$ and other peak-based intensity measures expected on arbitrary site conditions can be obtained from @eq-PGVS and @eq-AIS [-@Verri2017],[-@Verri2023a], where $F_o(v_S)$ is the multi-period site factor (@eq-AF) defined for a target site in terms of $\bar v_S$, $pga^{o}$ is the peak-ground acceleration in rock, $\psi_1,\psi_2$ are model parameters.

$$pgv(v_S) \approx F_o(v_S) \ \phi_1 \ (pga^{o}/g)^{\phi_2} \  [m/s]$${#eq-PGVS}

$$ai(v_S) \approx F_o(v_S) \ \psi_1 \ (pga^{o}/g)^{\psi_2} \  [m/s]$${#eq-AIS}

> Spectral ordinates (design spectra) and peak-ground accelerations $pga$ obtained for the maximum design earthquake (MDE) under different site conditions are shown in @sec-DE_results.
